headline: Severe shortage: Dhaka now lives by the ‘gas clock’ as crisis deepens
summary: Residents across various areas of the capital are facing acute gas shortages, prompting protests from the Communist Party of Bangladesh (CPB).
details: Various areas of Dhaka are currently experiencing a severe gas crisis that has disrupted daily life for residents.
The shortage has become so acute that people are forced to manage their schedules around the limited availability of gas, leading to the term 'gas clock'.
The Communist Party of Bangladesh (CPB) has held protests demanding a swift resolution to the crisis.
The CPB has further demanded that gas bills should not be collected from consumers until the gas shortage is resolved.

headline: DU suspends 3 teachers and relieves 4 others of key duties
summary: The university syndicate decided on the actions following allegations of unprofessional behavior, moral turpitude, and activities contrary to the July uprising spirit.
details: The Dhaka University syndicate has suspended three teachers from their jobs and relieved four others of their administrative and academic responsibilities.
Among those suspended are Professor Dr. Sadeka Halim of the Sociology department, Professor Dr. Md. Shafiqul Islam and Professor Dr. Afroza Shelee of the Nuclear Engineering department.
The suspensions follow allegations of unprofessional behavior both inside and outside the classroom, as well as charges of moral turpitude.
Additionally, Professor Dr. Md. Abdul Muhit of the Clinical Pharmacy and Pharmacology department was relieved of his duties as chairman and all other academic and administrative roles.
Dr. Muhit was accused of activities contrary to the spirit of the July mass uprising, spreading anti-government and anti-administration propaganda, and supporting a banned organization.
The university administration has taken these actions based on reports from investigation committees and student complaints.
caption:
Three Dhaka University teachers have been suspended and four others stripped of their duties over various allegations.

The Dhaka University syndicate has suspended three teachers from their jobs and relieved four others of their administrative and academic responsibilities.

Among those suspended are Professor Dr. Sadeka Halim of the Sociology department, Professor Dr. Md. Shafiqul Islam and Professor Dr. Afroza Shelee of the Nuclear Engineering department.

The suspensions follow allegations of unprofessional behavior both inside and outside the classroom, as well as charges of moral turpitude.

Additionally, Professor Dr. Md. Abdul Muhit of the Clinical Pharmacy and Pharmacology department was relieved of his duties as chairman and all other academic and administrative roles.

Dr. Muhit was accused of activities contrary to the spirit of the July mass uprising, spreading anti-government and anti-administration propaganda, and supporting a banned organization.

The university administration has taken these actions based on reports from investigation committees and student complaints.
